clue.text: Modern poet, one of doubtful reputation

definitions.meaning: Dylan, the twentieth-century Welsh poet, bore this surname
the apostle who refused to believe in the Resurrection without proof gave his name to every sceptic: a 'doubting' one

explanation.surface: Description of a contemporary poet whose reputation is questionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan the Welsh poet shares his surname with the doubting apostle, proverbial for scepticism.

clue.text: It maintains circulation as newspaper boss suffers second loss

indicators.note: the boss suffers a loss, so one of his letters is taken away from the surname

parts.note: William Randolph Hearst was the American press magnate

explanation.surface: A newspaper owner keeps sales going despite losing his deputy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulation' suggests a newspaper's sales, which fits the press baron, but it is blood circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ that pumps blood keeps the body's circulation going.

clue.text: Historic craft has potential to flourish

parts.note: may expresses possibility, as in 'it may happen'
to flower is to bloom or thrive

explanation.surface: An old boat is said to be capable of thriving.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mayflower carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620, hence 'historic'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ship carrying the Pilgrims across the Atlantic is a famous vessel of history.

clue.text: Keep quiet, absorbed by religion

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
to be into something is to be absorbed by it, keen on it

explanation.surface: Someone stays silent, wrapped up in their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absorbed by' looks like a container signal, but it is the plain synonym INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: The indigenous faith of Japan, worshipping kami spirits, is a religion.

clue.text: Filled out a record for person who's resigned

parts.note: someone who has filled out has grown fat
a list is a written record

explanation.surface: A form is completed for someone who has quit their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resigned' suggests leaving a job; here it means accepting one's fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who believes events are predetermined accepts them with resignation.

clue.text: Academic representative, one with leftist sympathies

parts.note: a fellow is a senior member of a college
a commercial traveller is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A college don who is also an agent turns out to be left-leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a sympathiser with communism who is not a party member.

clue.text: End semester?

parts.note: a semester is a term, so its finish could whimsically be called a term's end, which is also a word for the last stop on a railway line

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for boundary is used for an end point, such as the final station of a line.

clue.text: It's okay, in short, to make rapid strides

definitions.meaning: a clipped form of legitimate, slang for genuine or acceptable

explanation.surface: Abbreviated reassurance that it is fine to walk quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang abbreviation of legitimate means above board; as a two-word phrase it means run fast.

clue.text: Replacement's taken over batsman's position in ground

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, on top of, the second

parts.note: a sub is a substitute or replacement
a batsman's stance is how he stands at the crease in cricket

explanation.surface: A substitute player has stepped into a cricketer's place on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a cricket ground; it means the basis or grounds of an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: The substance of an argument is its basis, the ground it rests on.

clue.text: Young man likely to misbehave? Right

definitions.text: Young man likely to misbehave? Right

parts.words: Young man likely to misbehave? Right
parts.note: a playful description of a charming seducer of women, with the sardonic 'Right' agreeing that such a man is indeed trouble

explanation.definitionFit: A man who habitually charms and seduces women is notorious for misbehaving with them.

clue.text: One area that's wet? Quite the reverse

definitions.text: One area that's wet? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: the phrase tells the solver to turn the letters round, and also that the place is the opposite of wet

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a bog is a wet, marshy area

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about a wet region answered with a flat contradiction.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Asian desert is an area that is the very opposite of wet.

clue.text: Weapon fired back in fight

indicators.note: the turned word is placed inside the word for a fight

parts.note: a set-to is a brief fight

indicators.note: back says the word for fired is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: lit means set alight, fired

explanation.surface: A gun goes off in reply during a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weapon fired back' paints a gunfight, but 'fired' means set alight and 'back' reverses it; the weapon is a dagger, not a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A short dagger with a slender blade is a weapon.

clue.text: Completely fitting parts of Bible within one old case

indicators.note: the two testaments go inside the letters for one and old, which form a case around them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
NT and OT, the New and Old Testaments, are the two parts of the Bible

explanation.surface: Bible sections fit neatly inside an antique box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' and 'case' complete the picture of the I and O enclosing NT and OT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in its entirety, wholly.

clue.text: Sailing vessel at Land's End — in what condition?

indicators.note: the end of the word Land is its final letter

parts.note: how asks in what state something is, as in 'how are you?'

explanation.surface: Someone asks the state of a ship lying off Cornwall's tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost point of Cornwall, England, which the surface trades on.
explanation.definitionFit: The lateen-rigged boat of the Arabian Sea is a sailing vessel.

clue.text: Paganism appears to inflame king

parts.note: to heat is to inflame
Henry is the name of eight English kings

explanation.surface: Pagan worship seems to stir up a monarch's anger.
explanation.definitionFit: The state or practices of unbelievers outside the main faiths is paganism.

clue.text: Moving about

explanation.surface: Something in motion around a place.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both emotionally affecting and concerning, as in 'matters relating to tax'.

clue.text: Big numbers dismantling apartheid

indicators.note: taking apart the word apartheid so its letters can be rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Large crowds are taking down a system of racial segregation.
explanation.definitionFit: The chart of best-selling records lists the biggest songs.

clue.text: Drink editor decisively finished off

parts.note: scotch is whisky

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor's whisky sees off the day's work.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour or plan is to put a firm end to it.

clue.text: Name dropping aristocratic female

indicators.note: the letter for name is dropped from the word for aristocratic

parts.note: patrician means noble, aristocratic

explanation.surface: A posh woman who name-drops.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Name-dropping' as one word; split it, Name is N and dropping removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman's name is a feminine given name, standing for a female.

clue.text: Attach to river bank

parts.note: to tie is to attach

explanation.surface: Fastening a boat to the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests a riverside; it means a row, as in a bank of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of seats or keys is a row, one level of a series.

clue.text: Constituent on the way from the City to Westminster

definitions.meaning: a single thread or element of a rope or argument

definitions.text: on the way from the City to Westminster
definitions.meaning: the London street running from the City financial district towards Westminster

explanation.surface: A voter travelling across central London.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is one component thread; the Strand is a London thoroughfare linking the City and Westminster.

clue.text: As long as one's left in the game

indicators.note: the letter for left is placed inside the name of the card game

parts.note: whist is a card game

explanation.surface: A player may continue while still in play.
explanation.walkthrough: Whist is an old card game for four players.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction means while, during the time that.

clue.text: Pound note in another currency

indicators.note: the note is put inside the name of the currency

parts.note: the lira was the currency of Italy
B is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A sterling banknote held in foreign money.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman pound weight gives the abbreviation lb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for a Roman pound weight is the source of lb.

clue.text: Drive off front of tee, as green has been shifted

indicators.note: the letters have been moved around into a new order
the first letter of the word tee

explanation.surface: A golfer drives from the tee after the green has been moved.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf misleads: 'front of' gives T, and 'has been shifted' rearranges T, AS and GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to drive them away from affection.

clue.text: Governor's first opportunity to prepare for office

indicators.note: the first letter of the word Governor

parts.note: room means scope or opportunity, as in room for improvement

explanation.surface: A governor gets his first chance to train for a post.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom someone is to train them up for a particular role.

clue.text: Cut, point by point

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
a nub is a point or knob

explanation.surface: A careful analysis made one point at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to ignore them pointedly, to rebuff them.

clue.text: Uproar produced in port by a bear

parts.note: Hull is a port in Yorkshire, England
Baloo is the bear in Kipling's The Jungle Book

explanation.surface: A commotion caused at a harbour by a bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy commotion is an uproar.

clue.text: Naval commander delays RN at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A captain postpones the Royal Navy's sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spartan admiral defeated Athens at Aegospotami in 405 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spartan general won the decisive sea battle of the Peloponnesian War.

clue.text: Delightful girl put on red slip

indicators.note: the girl's name follows, placed on the end of, the jumbled letters
a slip is an error, so the letters are mis-arranged

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A lovely young woman wearing a red petticoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' rearranges RED to DRE, and 'put on' adds AMY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lovely and soothing is called heavenly or delightful.
